title: Spanish translation, cross-cultural adaptation, and psychometric validation of the CATQ-S and FATQ-S: assessing motivational functions of online and face-to-face aggression in secondary school students.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peer aggression, both face-to-face and online, is a growing public health concern that affects adolescents' emotional wellbeing, social participation, and academic functioning. Understanding the motivational functions that sustain these behaviours is essential for designing effective school-based interventions.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and psychometrically validate the short Spanish versions of the Cyber Aggression Typology Questionnaire (CATQ-S) and the Face-to-Face Aggression Typology Questionnaire (FATQ-S), which assess four motivational functions of aggression in secondary school students.
METHODS: An instrumental, cross-sectional design was used. Following international guidelines for translation and cross-cultural adaptation, the instruments were translated, back-translated, and reviewed by an expert committee. Comprehensibility and perceived difficulty were examined in a sample of 96 secondary school students (ages 12-16). Psychometric validation was conducted in a separate sample of 1443 compulsory secondary education students (ages 11-16) from public schools in Extremadura, Spain. Confirmatory factor analyses, internal consistency indices, convergent validity, and measurement invariance across gender were assessed.
RESULTS: Both the CATQ-S and FATQ-S replicated the original four-factor structure with acceptable to good fit indices. Internal consistency and AVE-based convergent validity were satisfactory across factors, whereas discriminant validity was not uniformly supported because of substantial overlap between some motivational dimensions. Multigroup analyses showed configural, metric, scalar, and strict invariance by gender, indicating that the instruments function equivalently for boys and girls.
CONCLUSIONS: The Spanish versions of the CATQ-S and FATQ-S are brief, conceptually grounded instruments showing generally adequate psychometric properties for assessing motivational functions of peer aggression in Spanish-speaking secondary school students. Their use may support research and educational assessment of the motives underlying aggressive behaviour in school settings.
